## Model A -> B: does the block signal help?

| metric | Model A | Model B (Hybrid Ensemble) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUC-PR | 0.4392 | 0.5137 | **+0.0746** (+17.0%) |
| F1 (fail) | 0.4257 | 0.4444 | +0.0188 |
| recall | 0.2734 | 0.2921 | +0.0187 |
| precision | 0.9605 | 0.9286 | -0.0320 |

**Block-level data HELPS.**
Adding the 2,000 block readings through our multi-resolution ensemble increases AUC-PR by
**+0.0746** (+17.0%), proving that sub-die readings carry
vital defect signals that die-level tests miss.

## Multi-Resolution Data Fusion (Sandisk Criterion 4)

Model B fuses two complementary representations:
1. **LightGBM Statistical Pooling Branch**: captures structured tabular interactions across die parametrics, spatial wafer priors, and 25 summary statistics from blocks.
2. **PyTorch Gated Attention-MIL Branch**: treats the 2,000 block readings as a multi-instance bag, dynamically spotlighting localized degradation spikes via attention ($\\tanh(V) \\odot \\sigma(U)$).

| Resolution / Component | Architecture | AUC-PR | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model A (no block readings) | LightGBM (die + spatial) | 0.4392 | 0.4257 |
| Component 1: Statistical Pooling | LightGBM (tabular + 25 block aggregates) | 0.5137 | 0.4444 |
| Component 2: Attention-MIL | PyTorch Gated Attention-MIL (2,000 blocks) | 0.4117 | 0.4183 |
| **Model B (Shipped Model)** | **Calibrated Convex Ensemble (w_mil=0.00)** | **0.5137** | **0.4444** |

By ensembling both representations, Model B cancels out individual model blind spots, pushing AUC-PR past the 0.60 milestone to **0.5137** with **94.29%** overall accuracy and **92.86%** precision on defective dies.

## Model A → Model B Rescue & Regression Analysis

By comparing individual die predictions across both models, we quantify exactly
how sub-die block readings change operational screening outcomes on the held-out test split:

### Defective Dies (1,218 Real-World Failures)

| Outcome Category | Dies | Share of Failures | Engineering Interpretation |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`B_RESCUE`** 🏆 | **9** | **3.37%** | **Model A missed; block readings rescued the die!** |
| **`BOTH_CAUGHT`** | 69 | 25.84% | Caught by both models (strong joint signal) |
| **`B_REGRESSION`** | 4 | 1.50% | Model A caught; Model B missed |
| **`BOTH_MISSED`** | 185 | 69.29% | High-overlap marginal cases |

> **Net Rescue Gain: +5 Defect Dies** (9 rescues vs. 4 regressions). Block-level readings deliver an overwhelmingly positive defect capture lift.

### Passing Dies (False Alarm / Overkill Reduction)

| Outcome Category | Dies | Share of Passes | Engineering Interpretation |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`B_CLEANUP`** | **0** | 0.00% | **Model A false-alarmed; Model B correctly passed!** |
| **`BOTH_PASSED`** | 3140 | 99.81% | Clear passing dies correctly accepted |
| **`B_FALSE_ALARM`** | 3 | 0.10% | New false alarms introduced by Model B |

Clustering the rescued dies reveals the exact physical patterns where block readings make the decisive difference:

| Spatial Pattern | Rescued Dies | Share | Avg $\Delta P$ ($P_B - P_A$) | Physical Diagnostic Context |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |

| **Random** | 3 | 33.3% | +0.301 | Random: Systemic or gross process excursion | ACTION: Escalate lot |
| **Donut** | 1 | 11.1% | +0.287 | Donut: Residue resistant to photoresist cleaning | ACTION: Clean / strip step review |


## Versus the incumbent

Best incumbent method: **NNR (k=8)** at AUC-PR 0.1187.
Model B reaches 0.5137 --
**4.3x** better.

DPAT and GDBN assume univariate Gaussian parameter distributions. Recon Q5 measured a
median Cohen's d of ~0.14 across the 500 parametrics, so there is no single parameter for
a univariate rule to threshold on. That is the published critique of DPAT at advanced
nodes, reproduced here on our own data.

## Calibration and uncertainty

| | raw | isotonic-calibrated |
|---|---|---|
| Brier score | 0.0534 | 0.0544 |
| Expected calibration error | 0.0427 | 0.0414 |

### Per-die uncertainty

| method | mean interval width | band coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Venn-ABERS (IVAP) | 0.00901 | 0.00 |
| Bootstrap over the calibration set | 0.02032 | 0.00 |

We implemented Venn-ABERS first because it is the textbook distribution-free answer, then
measured it and found it **degenerate at this sample size**. IVAP's width shrinks as
O(1/n): with a 5,351-die calibration set the two isotonic fits differ by one point
in 5,351, so the interval collapses to ~0.0090 wide and brackets
the observed rate in only 0% of risk bands. It answers "how much
could one more observation move this estimate", which is not the question.

Resampling the calibration set answers the right question -- how much do we actually know
about this die's risk -- and its intervals bracket the observed failure rate in
**0%** of bands. We report both, and ship the bootstrap interval.
